newsitem.title: GERMANY: German shares drift to slightly higher IBIS close.
newsitem.headline: German shares drift to slightly higher IBIS close.

text.p: German shares ended a mostly directionless day's trade with minor gains on Monday, as interest in bank stocks helped offset general uncertainty about whether the market had ended its bull run.

The IBIS DAX index closed late electronic dealings up 9.92 points at 2,992.55 points, having pared earlier gains after a weak start on Wall Street. In the middle of the afternoon, the DAX had closed floor trade down 3.71 points at 2,994.53.

"The German equity market appears to be changing down several gears," said Trinkaus Capital Management in a commentary, noting that higher than expected January inflation, the apparent end to Wall Street's boom and Japanese equities' weakness were negatives for the market.
With little domestic news to distract them, dealers were focused on U.S. employment cost data due on Tuesday.

"Things will get going properly tomorrow," said a Munich dealer. "The U.S. numbers will give us a whole new picture of what stocks are up against in terms of (interest) rate prospects and it should be a better day for home news as well."
Bank shares led advancers from the start ahead of dividend announcements expected from tomorrow from the biggest players.
Deutsche Bank, the heaviest-traded of the blue chip stocks, ended IBIS trade up 1.21 marks at 85.22 marks.

Deutsche's supervisory board meets tomorrow, an event usually followed by a dividend announcement, and Commerzbank, which pared its gains to end the day up just nine pfennigs at 43.69 marks, is to reveal its 1996 dividend in the morning.
Steelmaker Thyssen AG closed up 3.40 marks at 290.40 marks, after the company issued full 1995/1996 results and said the overall outlook was positive.
